To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible for a social network to be assessed and ranked based on the links of the social network of the users, and the links of their exogenous interaction networks.

1) it is possible to assess and rank links of a social graph using only one exogenous interaction network, and 2) it is possible that using the structure of multiple exogenous interaction networks can help in the assessment and ranking of links of a social networks, but this depends on the classifiers used.

1) it is possible to assess the links of social networks using the structure of other interaction networks, and 2) the structure of multiple networks is better than the structure of a few networks for link classification and ranking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
link assessment and ranking in social networks, and we propose a novel approach to address these problems using external interaction networks.
link assessment and link strength ranking in online social networks.
the assessment and ranking of links in social networks using exogenous interaction networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the link classification and link strength ranking problem can be effectively tackled with the use of external interaction networks.
the use of exogenous interaction network data can be very useful in assessing the links of a network.
the link classification and tie strength ranking problem in social networks can be solved by employing a single exogenous interaction network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the link assessment and ranking problem can be addressed by using exogenous interaction networks and machine learning classifiers.
it is possible and effective to assess and rank the links in a network of interest by utilizing the structure of other interaction networks.
it is possible, using only the structure information of a single interaction network, to assess and rank the links in a given social network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
link classification and link strength ranking are possible using only the structure and the ground truth of the social network and the exogenous interaction network.
link assessment and link strength ranking in social networks is possible using only the structure (and not the content) of exogenous interaction data.
the assessment of the links in a single social network can be improved by using the structure of exogenous interaction network(s) and machine learning classifiers.
